blocks.question: Q1: You have lessons array 10 objects, each with id, title, xp. You want total XP if completed 2 lessons (id <=2). You write lessons.filter(l => l.id <= completed).reduce((t, l) => t + l.xp, 0) vs lessons.forEach(l => { if (l.id <= completed) total += l.xp }). Which returns total XP and difference?
options: Both same but filter+reduce returns new array not total, forEach returns total

filter+reduce: filter returns array of 2 completed lessons, reduce accumulates xp 100+100=200 returns 200 total XP number. forEach: loop, if id <= completed add xp to total variable, total 200 but needs external variable. filter+reduce functional returns total directly, forEach imperative needs external total. Both 200 but filter+reduce one line returns total, forEach needs total variable outside
blocks.correctFeedback: Yes! Both 200 but filter+reduce returns total directly functional, forEach needs external variable imperative!
blocks.incorrectFeedback: filter(l=>l.id<=2) returns [lesson1, lesson2] array 2 lessons, reduce((t,l)=>t+l.xp,0) total 0+100=100, 100+100=200 returns 200. forEach if id<=2 total+=xp needs total variable outside, total 200 but not return. Both 200 but filter+reduce returns total, forEach needs external total.
blocks.reasoning: filter+reduce vs forEach for total XP - functional returns directly vs imperative needs external variable.

blocks.question: Q2: You have getStatus = (id, completed) => id <= completed? 'completed' : id === completed+1? 'current' : 'locked'. For completed=2, id=3 returns current, id=4 locked. What about id=2? And id=3 with completed=2 vs id=3 with completed=5?
options: id=2 completed, id=3 with completed=2 current, id=3 with completed=5 completed - because id <= completed true for 2<=2 completed, 3<=2 false, 3===3 true current, 4>3 locked. For id=3 with completed=5, 3<=5 true completed (already done), not current. Status depends on completed value
blocks.correctFeedback: Yes! Status depends on completed value - id=3 current when completed=2 (next lesson), completed when completed=5 (already done)!
blocks.incorrectFeedback: getStatus: id <= completed? completed : id === completed+1? current : locked. id=2, completed=2: 2<=2 true completed. id=3, completed=2: 3<=2 false, 3===3 true current. id=3, completed=5: 3<=5 true completed (already completed, not current). Status changes with completed value.
blocks.reasoning: getStatus depends on completed - same id different status based on completed value.

blocks.question: Q3: You render 10 lessons. Direct append in loop: container.appendChild(card) each iteration 10 reflows. Grid method: grid in memory, forEach grid.appendChild(card) no reflow, container.appendChild(grid) 1 reflow. Which faster and why grid div also needed for CSS?
options: Grid 1 reflow 10x faster than 10 reflows - build in memory no reflow then append once. Also grid div has CSS grid-template-columns: repeat(2, 1fr) for 2-column layout, without grid div no grid layout cards stack vertical. Your dashboard uses grid method efficient and correct layout
blocks.correctFeedback: Yes! 1 reflow 10x faster and grid div needed for CSS grid 2 columns!
blocks.incorrectFeedback: Direct append: Each appendChild reflow layout recalc 10 times slow. Grid: Append to grid in memory not in DOM no reflow, append grid once 1 reflow fast. Grid div class lesson-grid CSS grid-template-columns 2 columns needed for layout.
blocks.reasoning: Reflow performance and CSS grid layout - grid method efficient and layout correct.

blocks.text: PAGE 9: Final Exam - Tricky Close Options

blocks.question: Q7: You have lessons array, completed=2. You want count completed. Option A: lessons.filter(l => l.id <= completed).length Option B: let count=0; for (let i=0; i<=lessons.length; i++) { if (lessons[i].id <= completed) count++ } Option C: lessons.reduce((c, l) => l.id <= completed? c+1 : c, 0) Which correct and which has bug?
options: A correct filter returns array length 2, C correct reduce counts 2, B buggy off-by-one i<=lessons.length goes to index 5 out of bounds lessons[5] undefined error, should i < lessons.length not i <= length. A and C functional correct, B imperative buggy off-by-one
A wrong - filter returns not count
blocks.correctFeedback: Yes! A filter+length correct, C reduce correct, B off-by-one bug i<=length goes out of bounds!
blocks.incorrectFeedback: A: filter(l=>l.id<=2) returns [lesson1, lesson2] length 2 correct. C: reduce counts c+1 if id<=2 else c, returns 2 correct. B: for i=0; i<=lessons.length; i++ goes to index 5 when length 5, lessons[5] undefined, lessons[5].id TypeError. Should i < length. A and C correct, B buggy.
blocks.reasoning: Filter+length vs reduce vs for loop off-by-one bug - A and C correct functional, B buggy <= vs <.
